slides.eyebrow: No one talks about this on a home tour
slides.sub: After 6 years in real estate, here are the 3 radon checks I'd make before any NJ closing.

slides.label: EPA radon action level
slides.body: That's 4 pCi/L (picocuries per liter). EPA says to fix a home at 4 or higher, and to consider fixing it between 2 and 4.
slides.source: EPA, What is EPA's Action Level for Radon (Oct. 2026)

slides.title: Ask for the seller's radon records
slides.body: In NJ, if the home was tested, the seller has to give you the results and proof of any mitigation when you sign the contract.

slides.title: Test during your inspection
slides.body: Only state-certified companies can test for radon in NJ. Ask your inspector if they're certified, or hire a certified tester.

slides.title: If it's high, ask about mitigation
slides.body: A certified mitigation company installs a fan that vents radon outside. NJDEP says these systems typically cut exposure by more than 90%. Talk to a real estate attorney about your situation.

caption:
No one talks about this on a home tour: radon. You can't see it or smell it, so the only way to know is to test.

EPA recommends fixing a home at 4 pCi/L or higher. In New Jersey, ask for the seller's radon records, test during your inspection with a state-certified company, and if the number is high, ask about mitigation before you close.

Talk to a real estate attorney about your situation.
